title: The text reflects on the legacy of General Sani Abacha following his death, portraying him as a controversial figure in Nigeria's history. While some viewed him as a tyrant who brought suffering and repression, others saw him as a strong leader who stepped in during a time of political chaos. Abacha's rule was marked by broken promises and increasing public alienation, leading to a fractured nation. The author emphasizes the urgent need for his successor, General Abdulsalam Abubakar, to address the deep-rooted issues in Nigeria, calling for a fundamental re-engineering of the country rather than a return to business as usual. The text highlights the challenges ahead for Abubakar, including the need to release political prisoners and distance himself from those responsible for Nigeria's past troubles.
